## Summary

This is the **spring-petclinic-rest** project (`org.springframework.samples.petclinic`). Owner request DTOs are **generated at build time** by the OpenAPI Generator from `src/main/resources/openapi.yml` — there are no hand-written `OwnerFieldsDto.java` / `OwnerDto.java` files in the tree. Everything routes through the single endpoint `POST /api/owners` (plus `PUT` for update).

### 1. Owner entity & email field
- **`/home/daniel/sandbox/src/main/java/org/springframework/samples/petclinic/model/Owner.java`**
  - Package `org.springframework.samples.petclinic.model`, JPA `@Entity @Table(name = "owners")`, extends `Person`.
  - Email field (lines 52-54):
    ```java
    @Column(name = "email")
    @Email
    private String email;
    ```
  - Note: only `@Email` (jakarta.validation) — no `@NotEmpty`, so email is optional. Also has `hasEmail()` helper (lines 118-120). Other constrained fields: `address`/`city` `@NotEmpty`, `telephone` `@NotEmpty @Pattern(E.164)`.

### 2. Controllers that create/update owners
- **`.../rest/controller/v1/OwnerRestControllerV1.java`** — package `...rest.controller.v1`, implements generated `OwnersApi`, `@RequestMapping("/api")`.
  - `addOwner(OwnerFieldsDto)` (lines 178-205) → `POST /api/owners`. This is the create path. Email is canonicalized at line 187: `owner.setEmail(emailNormalizer.normalize(owner.getEmail()));`
  - `updateOwner(Integer, OwnerFieldsDto)` (lines 209-222) → also normalizes email (line 219).
  - `@InitBinder("ownerFieldsDto")` (lines 146-149) registers `ownerFieldsValidator` and `postcodeValidator` on the binder so they run during the `@Valid` pass.
- **`.../rest/controller/v2/OwnerRestControllerV2.java`** — implements `OwnerV2Api`; only exposes `listOwnersPage(...)` (read/paging). No create/update here.

### 3. Bean Validation constraints / custom validators on owner email
- Declarative: `@Email` on `Owner.email` (entity). The generated `OwnerFieldsDto` also carries constraints from `openapi.yml` → `OwnerFields.email` has `format: email` and `maxLength: 255` (lines 2039-2047). Generated DTO getters get `@jakarta.validation.constraints.Email` + `@Size(max=255)`.
- **`.../rest/controller/EmailNormalizer.java`** — `@Component`, trims + lower-cases email, returns `null` when blank. Canonicalization only, not validation.
- **No existing email blocklist / disposable-domain validator exists.** The only reference to "blocklist"/"mailinator"/"disposable" in the whole tree is the failing test (see item 6).
- Custom validators for other owner fields (models for how to add one) live in `.../rest/controller/`:
  - Binder-registered `Validator` style (surfaces via BindingResult → 400): `OwnerFieldsValidator.java`, `PostcodeValidator.java`.
  - Service/exception style (throws → mapped by advice): `CityCapacityValidator`, `DailyRegistrationLimitValidator`, `HouseholdDuplicateValidator`, `RegistrationDateValidator`, plus paired exceptions (`*Exception.java`), and `InvalidTelephoneException`.

  Binder-style example (`PostcodeValidator`, rejects into `Errors`):
  ```java
  @Override public boolean supports(Class<?> c){ return OwnerFieldsDto.class.isAssignableFrom(c); }
  @Override public void validate(Object t, Errors e){
      OwnerFieldsDto owner=(OwnerFieldsDto)t; ...
      e.rejectValue("postcode","postcode.outOfRange","postcode is not valid...");
  }
  ```

### 4. How validation errors become HTTP 400
- **`.../rest/advice/ExceptionControllerAdvice.java`** (`@ControllerAdvice`).
  - `@ExceptionHandler(MethodArgumentNotValidException.class)` (lines 223-259): this catches all `@Valid`/binder validation failures (Bean Validation + binder-registered `Validator`s like `OwnerFieldsValidator`/`PostcodeValidator`). Returns `HttpStatus.BAD_REQUEST` as an RFC-7807 `ProblemDetail`, attaching `schemaValidationErrors` and `errors` (list of field names).
  - Business-rule exceptions get their own handlers, e.g. `InvalidTelephoneException` → 400 (lines 143-149), `FutureRegistrationDateException` → 400 (208-214), `HouseholdDuplicateException`/`CityCapacityExceededException` → 409, `DailyRegistrationLimitExceededException` → 429.
- `@Valid` itself is applied on the generated `OwnersApi` interface method params (from openapi.yml `requestBody` refs), so the controller's `OwnerFieldsDto` parameter is validated automatically.

### 5. DTOs / request bodies for owner creation
- **Generated** from `/home/daniel/sandbox/src/main/resources/openapi.yml`:
  - `OwnerFields` schema (lines 1991-2090) → generates `OwnerFieldsDto` (create/update request body; email at 2039-2047; `sharesHousehold` write-only flag at 2077-2086; required: firstName, lastName, address, city, telephone).
  - `Owner` schema (allOf OwnerFields + read-only fields) → `OwnerDto` (response).
  - Generation via `openapi-generator-plugin` (version property line 35 of `pom.xml`). The concrete `*.java` DTOs live under `target/generated-sources/...` after a build, in package `org.springframework.samples.petclinic.rest.dto`.
- Mapping entity↔DTO: **`.../mapper/OwnerMapper.java`** (MapStruct) — `toOwner(OwnerFieldsDto)` (line 113), `toOwnerDto(Owner)` (line 49). Email is mapped implicitly (no explicit `@Mapping` override, so name-matched).

### 6. Owner-related tests + validation style
- **`.../src/test/java/org/springframework/samples/petclinic/acceptance/AcceptanceBase.java`** — black-box MockMvc base. Key helpers: `ownerNode()` builds a fully-valid unique owner (firstName/lastName/address/city/telephone; no email by default), `createOwner(body)` does `POST /api/owners`, `createOwnerOk`, `getOwner`/`fetchOwner`. `@SpringBootTest @AutoConfigureMockMvc @Transactional @WithMockUser(roles OWNER_ADMIN,...)`. Uses `tools.jackson` (Jackson 3) `ObjectMapper`/`ObjectNode`.
- **`.../src/test/java/org/springframework/samples/petclinic/acceptance/AcceptanceTest.java`** — currently contains one test that is the **target spec** ("email-blocklist: Reject with 400 when the owner's email domain is on a disposable-domain blocklist"):
  ```java
  @Test
  void errorRejectsDisposableDomain() throws Exception {
      ObjectNode o = ownerNode();
      o.put("email", "x@mailinator.com");
      createOwner(o).andExpect(status().isBadRequest());
  }
  ```
  Validation-test style: build an `ObjectNode`, override the field under test, POST, assert `status().isBadRequest()`.

## What I changed

The spec: reject with **400** when an owner's email domain is on a disposable-domain blocklist (`mailinator.com`, `tempmail.com`, `guerrillamail.com`).

I followed the codebase's established binder-registered `Validator` pattern (the same one `PostcodeValidator` uses), which surfaces failures through the standard `@Valid` / `BindingResult` path that `ExceptionControllerAdvice` already maps to a 400.

1. **New `DisposableEmailDomainValidator`** (`rest/controller/DisposableEmailDomainValidator.java`) — a single-responsibility Spring `Validator` for `OwnerFieldsDto`. It extracts the email's domain (case-insensitively, trimmed) and rejects the `email` field when it matches the blocklist. It's a no-op when no email is present, so the field stays optional.

2. **Wired it into `OwnerRestControllerV1`** — added the import, constructor injection, and registered it on the existing owner binder alongside `ownerFieldsValidator` and `postcodeValidator`. This automatically covers both create (`POST`) and update (`PUT`), since both bind `ownerFieldsDto`.

No existing logic was duplicated — email canonicalization stays in `EmailNormalizer`, syntactic checks stay on the `@Email` constraint, and the new blocklist rule lives in its own small unit.
